answer: The Management program prepares students in management and administration with a curriculum balancing theory and practice. The BBA in Management requires 99 credits.

Management mandatory courses: BADM 410 International Business (Senior Standing), BADM 485 Co-op, BADM 490 Entrepreneurship, BECN 305 Managerial Economics (BECN 301), BHRM 300 Human Resources Management (BMGT 200), BMGT 205 Organizational Behavior (BMGT 200), BMGT 300 Project Management (Junior Standing), BMGT 400 Operations Management (BADM 250), and BMGT 485 Strategic Management (Senior Standing).

source_quote: must study 3 credit hours of major electives. Major electives could be upper-level courses
answer: Management students take 3 credits of major electives, e.g., BADM 480 Independent Studies, BFIN 400 Financial Management II, BMGT 410 Quality Management, BMKA 365 Sales Management, or BMKA 450 Event Marketing and Management.

answer: Management students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (BADM 485) with faculty follow-up, reports, posters and presentations; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites. The program text says Co-op is typically completed in the summer of the second year, while the study plan places it in the Year 3 summer.
review_note: p.244 says Co-op is typically in the summer of the second year; the study plan (p.247) and all other programs place it after the third year.

answer: Management graduates are eligible for entry-level administrative positions in banking, insurance, tourism, retail, health, education, consultancy and industry, advancing to upper-level management; others pursue graduate study in HRM, supply chain, operations or retail management.

answer: Management outcomes: apply business knowledge in decision-making; apply managerial and entrepreneurial competencies to launch and manage a business; communicate effectively; analyze business problems; and respond to ethical dilemmas.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Business Administration in Management encompasses 99 credit hours
answer: The Management BBA spans six semesters and summer sessions (Community Engagement, Co-op). Year 1 Fall (16 cr): BACC 205, BADM 215, BITM 200, BMGT 200, ENGL 210, MATH 207. Year 1 Spring (16 cr): BACC 255, BADM 225, BADM 235, BADM 250, BMGT 205, ENGL 217.
Management Year 2 Fall (18 credits): BADM 230, BECN 301, BFIN 300, BHRM 300, BMKA 200, and a Science Elective.
Management Year 2 Spring (18 credits): BADM 355, BECN 302, BITM 300, BITM 350, BMGT 300, and a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective; then BADM 290 Community Engagement in the Year 2 summer.
Management Year 3 Fall (15 credits): ARAB 212, BADM 410, BADM 420, BMGT 400, a 1-credit Community & Sustainability course, and a Social Science Elective.
Management Year 3 Spring (15 credits): BADM 490, BECN 305, BMGT 485, a Major Elective, a Social Science Elective; Year 3 Summer: BADM 485 Co-op (1 credit).

source_quote: This course is a blend of lectures, case studies, and discussions of current global and
answer: BADM 410 International Business, 3(3,0): international business strategies and environments, international trade, investment and finance, country selection, export/import, FDI and global marketing. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: In addition to the principles of supply chain management, students learn advanced
answer: BMGT 400 Operations Management, 3(3,0): supply chain principles, forecasting, quality management, facility layout, inventory control, capacity and aggregate planning, JIT and statistical process control. Prerequisite: BADM 250.

source_quote: This course highlights that TQM has become crucial for business excellence in
answer: BMGT 410 Quality Management, 3(3,0): TQM, the seven quality tools, SPC, quality function deployment, reliability, Six Sigma, benchmarking, certification and quality costing. Prerequisite: BADM 250.

source_quote: helps students understand and apply practical interpersonal techniques and
answer: BMKA 365 Sales Management, 3(3,0): interpersonal and persuasive selling techniques, value-added strategies, customer value and long-term relationships. Prerequisite: BMKA 200; Junior Standing.

source_quote: A course on starting and operating a small business. It introduces the fundamentals
answer: BMGT 210 SME Management, 3(3,0), a course for non-business programs: starting and running a small business - planning, raising capital, managing employees, marketing, business plans and legal issues, at least one-third hands-on.
